UPDATE course_lessons SET content = REPLACE(content, '#### LEDs (Light Emitting Diodes)

LEDs are diodes that emit photons when forward-biased. In industrial control panels, they are ubiquitous for status indication (Power ON, Fault, Input Active, Network Link). They require a series resistor to limit current; otherwise, they will draw too much current and instantly burn out. Never connect an LED directly to a 24VDC source without a current-limiting resistor.', '#### LEDs (Light Emitting Diodes)

LEDs are diodes that emit photons when forward-biased. In industrial control panels, they are ubiquitous for status indication (Power ON, Fault, Input Active, Network Link). They require a series resistor to limit current; otherwise, they will draw too much current and instantly burn out. Never connect an LED directly to a 24VDC source without a current-limiting resistor.

#### Photodiodes & Optocouplers

A photodiode is the reverse of an LED — it converts incoming light into electrical current. In industrial automation, photodiodes are most commonly found inside **optocouplers** (also called opto-isolators), which provide galvanic isolation between high-voltage power circuits and low-voltage control logic. An optocoupler packages an LED and a photodiode/phototransistor in a single DIP or SMD package. When the LED side is energized by the control circuit, it emits infrared light across a tiny gap. The photodiode on the other side detects this light and generates a proportional current, passing the signal without any electrical connection between the two sides.

Optocouplers are critical in:
- **PLC output modules:** Every transistor output card uses optocouplers to isolate the processor backplane from field wiring
- **VFD control boards:** Gate drive circuits use optocouplers to isolate the low-voltage DSP from the high-voltage IGBT gates
- **Communication interfaces:** RS-485 isolated transceivers use optocouplers to prevent ground loops between networked devices

> **Failure Mode:** Optocoupler LEDs degrade over time (especially at elevated temperatures), reducing their light output until the photodiode can no longer reliably detect the signal. This causes intermittent "ghost" signals — outputs that work sometimes but not others, or communication that drops packets randomly. Replacement is the only fix.

#### Power Freewheeling Diodes (IGBT/MOSFET Protection)

In VFD output stages and servo drives, each IGBT or MOSFET switching element has a high-power freewheeling diode connected anti-parallel (reverse-biased during normal conduction). These diodes provide a path for inductive motor current to flow when the switching device turns off. Without them, the inductive kickback from the motor windings would destroy the semiconductor switches instantly. These are NOT standard 1N4007 diodes — they are specialized fast-recovery power diodes rated for 30-600A and designed to switch in nanoseconds. When one fails (usually shorts), it takes out the entire IGBT module and often the gate drive circuitry as well.') WHERE id = 60013;
